title: SPARC Listening Session: National Priorities for Open Education
content:
"SPARC invites you to participate in an interactive listening session for the Open Education National Priorities Process (http://opened.org/national-priorities), a collaborative effort to develop advocacy priorities and action plans for open education in the U.S. for the next three years. The session will begin with a brief overview of the process, invite discussion and brainstorming about the challenges facing education today and where openness fits in, and conclude with optional breakout discussions to dive deeper. Output from the session will inform a national conversation that continues throughout the fall. 

This session is hosted by SPARC in collaboration with the Open Education Association."

title: From access to impact: the gold OA advantage | Springer Nature
content:
"This white paper explores the effect of different routes to OA on the reach and impact of articles in hybrid journals. The data shows that, 8 years on from our first major study into this topic, there is still a substantial advantage for gold OA articles across all disciplines (measured by downloads, citations and Altmetric Attention Score) over both non-OA articles and green OA articles. 4

The analysis of 204,781 articles published in 1,812 hybrid Springer Nature journals in 2023 also shows how gold OA can accelerate the number of downloads over time and the diversity of geographic readership, leading to faster impact and greater equity in access."

title: Gold OA reaches record 44pc share of global research output - Research Information
content:
"Gold open access (OA) articles reached their highest-ever share of global research output in 2025, accounting for 44% of all journal articles, reviews and conference papers published worldwide.

Nearly two million research articles were published through gold OA during the year, making it the principal driver of immediate, freely available access to research, according to the latest release of the STM Open Access Dashboard.

The Dashboard, which tracks the uptake of different routes to OA between 2015 and 2025, shows that gold OA has quadrupled over the past decade."

title: Open Access Library and Information Science (LIS) Journals Indexed in the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ): An Analytical Study | Annals of Library and Information Studies
content: Abstract: The study examines the trends and current status of Open Access (OA) research journals listed in the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ) in the field of Library and Information Science (LIS) from 2003 to mid-2026. It investigates the profile of OA LIS journals, publishing trends, publishing practices, open access policies, licensing practices and journal scope through thematic analysis of keywords. The study identified 231 OA LIS journals published in 32 languages by 200 publishers across 55 countries globally. The study adopted a descriptive research approach and data were collected from the DOAJ and verified through the official journal websites where required. The collected data were compiled, organised, tabulated and analysed using Microsoft Excel. The findings provide insights into the growth of LIS journals, geographical distribution, publishers, language profile, publication mode, peer-review practices, article processing charges (APCs), copyright ownership, Creative Commons licensing, self-archiving policies, digital preservation mechanisms, Digital Object Identifier (DOI) availability and other publishing infrastructure adopted by OA LIS journals.

title: Perceived ease of access and use of open access resources by library and information science postgraduate students in south-west Nigeria
content: Abstract: Thi study examined Perceived Ease of Access (PEOA) and Use of Open Access Resources (OAR) by Library and Information Science (LIS) postgraduate students in universities in Southwest, Nigeria. The study adopted a quantitative research method and correlational research design to answer two research questions and one hypothesis. The population consisted of 227 postgraduate students from five universities: Adeleke University (AU) - 22, Babcock University (BU)-35, Lead City University (LCU)-30, Tai Solarin University (TASUED)-30 and University of Ibadan (UI)-110. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered through the total enumeration technique. The collected data were analysed using both descriptive and inferential statistical methods. The findings revealed that the largest respondents were: UI (49%), females (50.7%), age group 26-30 (39.4%), and single (55.9%). OARs were used mostly for research work (=3.60); group/individual practical purposes (=3.34) personal tutorials (=3.26) and examination preparation (=3.24). title: Strengthening Trust and Leadership: Reflections on National Institutes of Health (NIH) 2026 Community Days: Securing NIH Controlled-Access Data and Our Data Protection Journey | Data Science at NIH
content: "On April 13 and 14, I had the privilege of leading the National Institutes of Health (NIH) 2026 Community Days: Securing NIH Controlled-Access Data webinars to engage directly with our stakeholders, researchers, and the broader public about the critical work we’re undertaking to protect controlled-access data. These sessions were designed to foster transparency around our security and operational standards, update the community on new resources and requirements, and reinforce our shared responsibility in safeguarding participant trust. I am deeply grateful for the vibrant participation and thoughtful questions that were raised, which underscores the importance and urgency of our mission. Protecting participants’ trust requires one standard: secure, consistent protections for NIH controlled-access data—whether it is processed within a NIH Controlled-Access Data Repository (CADR) or a research institution’s IT systems. This principle drove the Extramural Community Days agenda, where we discussed not only what needs to be done, but why rigorous data protection is more essential than ever. title: Kirsch | Assessing Researcher Data Sharing Practices Using Publicly Available Dataset Metadata: A Reproducible Workflow for Institutional Stakeholders | Journal of Librarianship and Scholarly Communication
content: Abstract: Introduction: Scholarly communities are experiencing increased emphasis on research data sharing and reuse. Given the range of available data repositories and variability in the use of persistent identifiers (PIDs) for individuals and institutions, aggregating datasets by researchers at a specific institution is a significant challenge. We developed a reproducible workflow to evaluate 1) data repository use by researchers at our institutions, 2) metrics of reuse, and 3) quality of metadata records. Methods: We used the DataCite REST API to locate metadata records for datasets with creator affiliation names that matched our institutions. We performed substantial cleaning and deduplication before comparing repository use, citations, usage metrics, and metadata completeness. Results: The most common data repositories were Dryad, Harvard Dataverse, figshare, Zenodo, ICPSR, and one institution’s institutional repository. View, download, and citation counts were available from a limited number of repositories, with some discrepancies between different citation reporting methods. The 2-year grant will accelerate OJC’s development, including building core technical features that leverage current open infrastructure. These comprise usage dashboards for libraries and authors, financial reporting tools, and a community engagement hub for journals and publishers. It will also support the legal and financial groundwork needed to share raised library funds equitably and transparently across OJC’s journals collections."

title: Wiley research publishing revenue jumps 12pc on OA growth and Emerald acquisition - Research Information
content:
"Wiley has reported 4% growth in its research division for the first quarter of its 2027 financial year, with publishing revenue climbing 12% as strong demand for open access and the addition of Emerald Publishing boosted the business.

Research revenue reached $293 million for the three months ended 31 July 2026, up 4% both on a reported basis and at constant currency.

Research Publishing revenue increased 12% at constant currency, driven by what Wiley described as strong growth in gold open access and AI licensing, alongside a $13 million contribution from Emerald Publishing following completion of the acquisition during the quarter.

The performance helped offset a 30% decline in Research Solutions revenue, which faced a tough comparison with the same period last year because of AI licensing income. Research Solutions generated $4 million in AI licensing revenue during the quarter, compared with $16 million a year earlier."

title: Project MUSE - The Data Rescue Project: A Crowdsourced Effort to Preserve At-Risk US Federal Data
content: Abstract: The US federal government is the world's largest data publisher. Since Trump's second inauguration, these data are threatened because their scope contravenes regime ideology and the offices that maintain these datasets no longer have adequate staff to preserve and provide access to the data. The Data Rescue Project was launched in 2025 as a community response to this crisis. We organized volunteers to work on data rescues, focusing especially on social data to fill an identified gap in other rescue efforts and emphasizing curation of the datasets for long-term data preservation. Through community-building, we became a coordinating body for the data rescue movement, streamlining communication and preventing duplication of effort in the US and internationally. In this article, we use the Data Rescue Project as a case study on building coalitions to push back against the destruction of digital information. Moreover, the US is not unique in its need for these efforts. The need to rapidly capture data from natural disasters, war zones, or unforeseen crises is a component of the digital preservation ecosystem that has been undercovered in the existing literature. content: "The 3-D digitization will take pictures all around the object and process them, using a photogrammetric procedure which identifies common features in the different images. The process orients the images in space and then performs what’s called the calibration of the camera, Guidi said. Once these steps are completed, image matching will automatically generate a dense cloud of 3-D points. This leads to generating the mesh, which is the model, the shape of the object, and its texture, he said. “You have to take several photographs around the object, and then you merge them and you process them in such a way…(that) gives you a digital twin of the physical object,” he said. “A digital twin means that also the size is totally the same, so it can be measured and analyzed, and this is very useful if you want to study something.” Possible challenges will be digitizing shiny or transparent objects because they are not compatible with the optical process used to generate the model. title: Altmetrics and Traditional Citation Impact among Top Iranian Researchers: A Comparative Analysis of ResearchGate and Academia
content: Abstract: Objective: The rapid expansion of digital communication has introduced alternative indicators of research visibility and impact, transforming traditional scholarly evaluation. This study investigates the potential of academic social networks for assessing the scholarly impact of Iranian researchers through an altmetrics approach. Method: This study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional design focused on the top 1% of Iranian researchers, as identified by the Islamic World Science Citation Center (ISC). Using a stratified sampling method, a sample of 203 researchers was selected across diverse disciplines. Data were collected between June 22, 2025, and June 4, 2026, by retrieving article-level metrics from Scopus, ResearchGate, and Academia.edu. Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient was applied to examine the relationship between Scopus citation counts and platform-specific engagement indicators (reads and views). Results: The analysis revealed a statistically significant positive correlation between Scopus citations and ResearchGate reads (r = 0.525).
